beats.narration: The request lands in the Onboarding inbox at 07:52 on Fri 6 Nov: roll over the full balance of member CS-1058220 to the "GW Family Superannuation Fund".
Olivia's agent extracts the request — full balance to an SMSF, a driver licence attached, and contact details changed by phone on 2 November.
Olivia opens case REQ-20261106-OPS002 and routes it to Benefits & Eligibility to check the rollover rules.
Ben checks the rollover against super law — any rollover to an SMSF must first pass the ATO SMSF verification service (SVS).
SVS fails: the SMSF's ABN is registered, but Grace's TFN isn't linked to it and the bank details and ESA don't match. Ben escalates to Financial Crime.

Felix rates the risk HIGH: contact details changed about 93 hours (under 96) before a full-balance rollover request, a new device on a Sydney IP while Grace's travel notice says Italy, an SMSF registered 9 days ago, a tampered driver licence and a payee-name mismatch.
Rory holds the SuperStream rollover — the 3-business-day clock only runs once all required information is received — and cancels the request with the receiving fund.
Theo approves the block, locks Grace's online access and refers the case for a suspicious matter report to AUSTRAC — a human decision, due within 3 business days.
Ben passes the blocked case to Payments to make sure nothing can leave the account.
Penny cancels the outbound rollover payment and confirms no funds leave Grace's account — the full $612,400 stays put.
Cara calls Grace on her previously verified mobile (0491 570 157). Grace confirms she never asked — her credentials are reset and a reassurance letter follows.

result.headline: Request blocked — Grace's super is safe
result.summary: Outcome: BLOCKED — fake SMSF rollover stopped; no funds left the account ($612,400 protected)
